content: Your doctor has prescribed dalteparin sodium, a medication classified as an anticoagulant or blood thinner, to help prevent the formation of harmful blood clots. This medication is administered via subcutaneous injection (under the skin) once daily. In some cases, dalteparin may be prescribed for other medical purposes; if you have questions about this, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Your healthcare provider will monitor the effectiveness of the treatment and check for potential side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is essential to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your body responds to the medication. Before starting dalteparin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to dalteparin, heparin, enoxaparin (Lovenox), other medications, or pork products. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking, especially those mentioned in the Important Warning section. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, diabetes, or any other significant medical conditions. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking dalteparin, contact your doctor immediately. Before administering dalteparin, carefully inspect the solution. It should appear clear and free of any floating particles. Check the container for leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the container is damaged. Instead, use a new solution and show the defective one to your healthcare provider. It is crucial to follow your healthcare provider's instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. Dalteparin may cause side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience an upset stomach that is severe or persistent. If you develop any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor or healthcare provider immediately: unusual bleeding, vomiting or coughing up blood or material resembling coffee grounds, bloody or black tarry stools, blood in your urine, red or dark-brown urine, easy bruising, excessive menstrual bleeding, fever, dizziness, or lightheadedness. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Your healthcare provider will likely supply you with several days' worth of dalteparin at a time and provide instructions on how to store it properly. Typically, the medication should be stored at room temperature. Always store medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will also instruct you on the proper disposal of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If you are receiving dalteparin via subcutaneous injection, be aware of the signs of a catheter-related infection at the injection site. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you notice tenderness, warmth, irritation, drainage, redness, swelling, or pain near the infusion site. Dalteparin is sold under the brand name Fragmin®.
